correctness.rationale: Gaussian change of measure gives h_s(u)=sqrt(s)exp((1-s)Phi^-1(u)^2/2)1_{u>=Phi(z/sqrt s)}. Mills ratio gives near-endpoint v^{-beta}(log(1/v))^{-beta/2} with beta=1-s, and interval-by-interval centering yields an L1-convergent endpoint sum; for beta<1/2 the proof extends L2 for the variance series. The first interval has the stated Pareto tail while the other centered intervals are uniformly bounded by a summable oscillation bound. At p beta=1 the remaining (log)^{-1/2} singularity causes divergence. For s>=1, only the indicator jump cell has nonvanishing n-scaled variance, and its Bernoulli phase follows exactly; smooth-cell oscillations vanish. Independent exact Gaussian cell moment computation verified all tested s=1 Bernoulli phases and s>1 asymptotic phases, not the limit distribution itself.
residual_risks: Threshold and variance fixed as n grows, no adaptive proposals or multivariate events.
The infinite series and tail asymptotics rest on analytic oscillation/Potter bounds, not numerical tests.
